United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

description.narrative:
Cameroon is suffering the effects of four complex and simultaneous humanitarian crises. These include the influx of Nigerian refugees in the Far North region and internal displacement due to Boko Haram since 2014, the influx of Central African refugees in the East and Adamawa regions since 2012, the socio-political crisis in the North-West and South-West regions since 2017 and the impact of the health crisis linked to the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the 2021 Humanitarian Needs Overview (data used during project design in 2021), approximately 4.4 million people required emergency assistance. In the area of education, access of 1.9 million school-aged girls and boys to education is hindered due to the crises, despite joint efforts by government and her partners. Given this situation and after the visit of Education Cannot Wait (ECW) in Cameroon in June 2021, Cameroon was approved to benefit from a Multi-Year Resilience Program (MYRP) seed fund of 25 million USD. These funds aimed to strengthen the response to existing gaps and improve the resilience of affected communities, through focus on a humanitarian-development-peace nexus approach.
The MYRP is a multi-sectoral intervention in selected municipalities affected by various crisis, to enhance access to quality inclusive education for school aged boys and girls. The overarching objective is to provide an integrated and holistic support package to promote continuous and inclusive access to quality, safe education and protective environment for children and adolescents of school age affected by the different crises in Cameroon. It strategically opts for the communal approach, to develop and give visibility to ‘model municipalities where access to formal and vocational education, learning, protection, and education governance are enhanced through a multi-sectoral convergent approach. The MYRP aims at building the resilience of the Education and Vocational sector in Cameroon by acting on the wellbeing of pupils/students, teachers, and parents in communities, and by addressing the important emergency related bottlenecks as well as the structural challenges that negatively affect access to quality education for the most vulnerable children in Cameroon.
To advance gender equality and ensure that girls and boys affected by the multiple crises across Cameroon are able to receive an education in a safe, protective, healthy and inclusive environment, the MYRP recognizes that a dual approach is needed, ensuring that gender is effectively mainstreamed across the consortium’s interventions but also that gender targeted interventions are reaching the differentiated needs of girls in accessing education and realizing their full potential. The Consortium will ensure that interventions take a rights-based and girl-centered approach, promoting their voices, adapting and responding to their needs. Against this backdrop, UNESCO will intervene particularly in outcomes and outputs related to gender transformative education and governance and management of the education system.
